content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Summary:** T4C is a **deviation** in this eight-year outsourcing agreement.

- **Customer side (§11.1, p0187):** we do have a convenience right, but it costs a full year's notice plus a redacted percentage of Estimated Remaining Value, unamortized Conversion costs and disposition Expenses (deemed liquidated damages under §13.5) — well short of the fallback (60–90 days' notice; fee capped at three months' fees).
- **Vendor side (§10.2, p0180):** M&I may withdraw any non-Core Service "at any time" on 90 days' notice — a mid-term convenience exit. The 90-day notice element is already met verbatim; only the mid-term timing fails.
- **Target chosen:** fallback, not preferred — deleting the fee outright would require collateral rewrites of §11.2(A) and the §13.5 liquidated-damages acknowledgement.
- **Redline (validated, ok:true):** two surgical replaces — 90 days' notice with an aggregate three-months'-fees cap on all §11.1 termination amounts, and M&I's Service withdrawal made effective only at the end of the Term.
